source.title: Impacts of invasive ants on pollination of native plants are similar in invaded and restored plant communities

design: Ant-exclusion experiments and pollinator observations on four native plant species across eight granitic inselbergs on Mahe, including four restoration sites and four invaded controls.

source_native_results.pollination_pathway: flying flower visitors were the primary pollination pathway and ant contribution to fruit set was generally small
source_native_results.interaction_effect: invasive-ant presence reduced the number of flowers probed per visit in restored and unrestored communities
source_native_results.reproductive_effect: native plant reproduction was negatively affected by invasive-ant presence
source_native_results.context_result: the negative effect was similar in restored and unrestored plant communities

observed_chain: invasive-ant presence -> reduced legitimate flower probing -> reduced native plant reproduction
claim_boundary: This is an island experimental/context contrast rather than an inter-island evolutionary transition. It tests qualitative propagation from interaction disruption to reproduction, not a unique ABM mechanism and not a universal restoration effect.
